findings.quote: Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
findings.rationale: A one-month fee cap is far below our floor (12 months' fees / USD 1,000,000) and "without exception" would override the Excluded Claims regime already agreed in 21.3. We have restated the cap on our standard basis and preserved the carve-outs.

replacement.oldText: Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
replacement.newText: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the Fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] Our position is a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, and "without exception" cannot stand because indemnities, confidentiality, data-protection/security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sit outside the cap under 21.3. Fallback is a mutual 12-month fee cap with those carve-outs retained.

findings.quote: Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
findings.rationale: The indemnity is one-way and unlimited against us, with no Vendor IP indemnity at all. We have added the Vendor indemnity (IP, breach of law, data breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) and narrowed our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our own breach of law.

replacement.oldText: 20. INDEMNIFICATION 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
replacement.newText: 20. INDEMNIFICATION 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. 20.2 Customer shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Vendor against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of Applicable Law. 20.3 The indemnified Party shall give prompt notice of the claim, the indemnifying Party shall control the defence (no settlement imposing obligations on the indemnified Party without its consent), and the indemnified Party shall reasonably cooperate at the indemnifying Party's expense.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We require a Vendor indemnity covering third-party IP claims, Vendor's breach of law, Vendor-caused data breaches and Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with our indemnity limited to our own content and legal compliance. Indemnities sit outside the liability cap per 21.3.

findings.quote: During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
findings.rationale: An undefined 24-month post-term non-compete on our business is a walk-away item and directly contradicts Section 12.3. We have deleted it.

replacement.oldText: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the products or services we develop, buy or sell; this also conflicts with Section 12.3. If some protection is genuinely needed, we could look at a term-only restriction on a single named competing product, capped at 12 months, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.

findings.quote: Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
findings.rationale: Full-term exclusive dealing with no performance-based exit is a walk-away position and conflicts with Section 12.3. We have deleted it.

replacement.oldText: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
replacement.newText: 2.2 [Intentionally omitted.] Customer may procure services of any kind from any third party at its discretion.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We retain freedom to source from other suppliers. If exclusivity is commercially essential, our fallback is a single defined product category for 12 months, terminating automatically on any failure to meet service levels or delivery dates.

findings.quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
findings.rationale: A three-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right is a walk-away item and is inconsistent with our convenience-termination right in 9.4 and with Section 12.3. Narrowed to a single 12-month, reducible commitment with a true-up.

replacement.oldText: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
replacement.newText: 2.1 Customer's only volume commitment is the amount stated in the applicable Order Form for the then-current twelve-month term, which Customer may reduce on thirty days' written notice. Any shortfall is settled as a true-up of Fees for Services actually ordered and is not a penalty, and no commitment survives termination of the applicable Order Form.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We do not accept multi-year take-or-pay without an exit. Our fallback limits any commitment to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up instead of a shortfall penalty.

findings.quote: 13.1 Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.
findings.rationale: A licence revocable at Vendor's discretion that excludes Affiliates and contractors is a walk-away position and is inconsistent with 13.2 and 13.3. We have extended the grant and removed at-will revocability.

replacement.oldText: 13.1 Vendor grants Customer alone a non-transferable licence, revocable at Vendor's sole discretion, to use the Services without Affiliates or contractors.
replacement.newText: 13.1 Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates and its contractors acting on Customer's behalf a non-exclusive licence to access and use the Services during the applicable subscription term, terminable only in accordance with Section 13.3 and transferable to a successor under Section 24.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] The licence must cover our Affiliates and contractors and cannot be revocable at will; revocation should only follow an uncured material breach, as Section 13.3 already provides.

findings.quote: 19.2 For fifteen days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation; after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation.
findings.rationale: A 15-day conformance window with an express cut-off of all correction and refund duties falls below our 90-day floor and undercuts the remedy in 19.4. Extended to 90 days and removed the cut-off.

replacement.oldText: 19.2 For fifteen days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation; after that date Vendor has no correction or refund obligation.
replacement.newText: 19.2 For ninety days after delivery, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation, and Customer's remedies for nonconformity are as set out in Section 19.4.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We need at least 90 days of conformance warranty for deliverables with a real remedy; the blanket cut-off of correction and refund obligations is not acceptable and conflicts with Section 19.4.

findings.quote: 11.1 Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.
findings.rationale: Immediate deletion with no export or transition help is a walk-away item and contradicts 11.2 and 11.3. Replaced with transition assistance and data-return language.

replacement.oldText: 11.1 Immediately on termination Vendor shall discontinue all assistance and permanently delete Customer Data without offering an export or migration support.
replacement.newText: 11.1 Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall, at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six months at Vendor's then-current rates, and shall not delete Customer Data except in accordance with Sections 11.2 and 11.3.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] On exit we need our data back in a machine-readable format and up to six months of transition assistance; immediate deletion is a walk-away and is inconsistent with Sections 11.2 and 11.3.

findings.quote: Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment.
findings.rationale: No MFN obligation is imposed on Customer; Section 12.3 expressly disclaims one.

findings.quote: hiring any person who responds to general recruitment
findings.rationale: No non-solicit or no-hire binds Customer, and general recruitment is expressly preserved.

findings.quote: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor.
findings.rationale: Matches our preferred position: 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and no Vendor convenience right during a committed term.

findings.quote: renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal
findings.rationale: 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder and uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3% match our preferred position.

findings.quote: governed by the laws of the State of New York
findings.rationale: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in New York County courts and no foreign arbitration.

findings.quote: Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service.
findings.rationale: Customer has affiliate/successor assignment rights without consent, Vendor assignment requires our consent, and no change-of-control trigger runs against us.

findings.quote: Vendor hereby assigns to Customer all worldwide right, title, and interest in those Deliverables
findings.rationale: We own Customer Data and Deliverables, Vendor Technology is licensed back perpetually under 13.2, and joint ownership is excluded.

findings.quote: no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice
findings.rationale: Frequency, notice, off-site independent auditor, Vendor cost unless 5% underpayment, and no system access all match our preferred position.

findings.quote: professional errors and omissions insurance of USD 2,000,000, and cyber and privacy liability insurance of USD 5,000,000
findings.rationale: Coverage lines and limits meet our preferred position, with certificates on request.

findings.quote: Customer owes Fees only for conforming Services provided through the effective termination date
findings.rationale: No liquidated damages or termination penalty is payable by Customer; the only Customer-payable exposure was the take-or-pay commitment, addressed under MINCOMMIT.
